prompts: Shot 1 opens with establishing space, wide shot, eye-level with slight downward angle, slowly pushing in from the edge of a high-rise rooftop. Foreground shows rain-soaked railing and scattered droplets; background features layered neon buildings and hazy light spots. Composition places a young woman slightly off-center, standing still in starting position, single sword hanging at her side before slowly lifting it. Neon side-lighting outlines her silhouette and sword spine with cold highlights. Puddles reflect fragmented ad colors. Camera push-in synchronizes with her inhalation during the start-up motion.

Shot 2 hard-cut from previous shot, close-up, eye-level. Camera continues forward push and slight right pan from chest level, focusing on the sword hand, wrist, and side profile of the face. Shallow depth of field blurs background neon into flowing color patches. Still on the rooftop, but distance shortened sharply to emphasize detail. She completes cloud-hand wrist turn, elbow and shoulder coordination creating sword path, then executes a straight thrust. Blade slices through rain mist, forming a brief sharp bright trail. Wrist movement is precise, forearm muscles tighten, sleeve edges generate micro-air waves. Lighting continues with neon side-lighting; sword surface occasionally reflects flashing white from ad lights.

Shot 3 hard-cut from previous shot, close-up, overhead view. Camera follows her into a wet narrow alley from above, first short overhead tracking, then slight orbiting. Uses wall and ground reflections to create strong leading lines. Foreground shows dangling wires and dripping water; She continuously spins and draws flower patterns along the alley, steps compact yet stable, weight shifts clearly visible. Shoes glide over puddles, creating arcing water trails that ripple outward. Sword movements align coaxially with body rotation. Hair tips and sleeves show natural lag at end of spin. Overall lighting remains within neutral night tone and neon reflection balance. Wet walls reflect intermittent color blocks.

Shot 4 hard-cut from previous shot, medium shot, low-angle. Scene progresses logically to an elevated walkway. Camera tracks upward from low angle with brief zoom-in. Background includes upper traffic light strips and large ad screens. Walkway railings create depth perspective. Character reaches action climax: first holds lunge downward slash, sword creates clear descending trajectory, then uses waist and hips to turn and block. Motion is crisp and decisive. Front foot lands, shaking residual water. Ad screen reflection flashes across blade surface, creating a brief sharp highlight.

Camera initially focuses on her hand, guard, and slightly rising chest, then slowly pulls back to medium-close. The subject stands slightly right of center, with the distant end of the background faintly revealing the cool morning light of the stadium. Depth of field is moderate to ensure both the person and the practice sword are clearly visible. Soft natural light enters from the side of the tunnel, preserving realistic shadow layers on the face and wrists, while occasional side light creates brief glints along the edge of the sword. Her sleeve and hair strands show slight movement. The starting motion is controlled, with muscle force transmitted sequentially through the shoulder, elbow, and wrist.

The second shot cuts abruptly from the previous one to the trackside, using a low-angle, eye-level tracking shot that transitions from wide to medium. The red curved track and grass edge form horizontal leading lines. The subject enters from the left side of the frame, with the background showing the empty morning stands and sky not yet fully bright. The space is more open, allowing full release of the action’s explosive power. Lighting remains primarily natural, but side lighting more distinctly outlines the blade and outer arm contours, clearly capturing the movement of the hem and footfalls. She first steps forward to complete the advance, then performs cloud hands with the sword, rotating her wrist in a circular motion, drawing a smooth arc along the outer side of her body axis. Next, she spins and slashes downward, lowering her center of gravity and tapping the ground at the lowest point to leverage momentum, then quickly taps again and flicks upward. The kinetic chain transfers from ankle, knee, hip, through the shoulder and arm to the sword tip—explosive yet controlled. The hem and ends of her hair swing naturally with the spin, showing delayed motion. The camera initially tracks horizontally to keep her centered, then makes a small circular movement during the spin, tilts slightly down during the slash to follow the blade's descent, and quickly pulls back to a medium shot during the flick-up, enhancing speed and spatial displacement. The overall atmosphere remains quiet and concentrated.

The third shot transitions from the previous one via a brief fade-in/fade-out, shifting naturally to the central open area of the stadium. It uses a combination of close-up and extreme close-up shots at eye level with a slight upward angle. The subject is centered in the frame, with a small amount of blurred ground texture in the foreground and an open field with soft morning light in the background. The composition is tighter, with focus firmly locked on her upper body, sword-holding hand, and the tip of the blade. The overall tone remains neutral, with natural light as the base, supplemented by a subtle rim light from the side-rear to clean up the silhouette of the stopped blade and facial outline. Continuing the momentum from the previous shot, she lifts her knee and completes her form, bringing the sword-hand steadily back to a controlled position. The blade tip initially trembles slightly due to inertia, then gradually comes to rest. Her shoulders and back sink again, her gaze fixes forward, and she transitions from post-explosion tension to an inwardly gathered state, completing the closing of the motion. The camera first pulls back slightly to show her full retraction, then slowly pushes in to a close-up where the blade tip and eyes are both sharply in focus, capturing the final moment of stabilization. After securing her laces, she gently presses the tail of the board with her front foot to test its spring, which responds with a slight rebound. Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, transitioning to a wide low-angle eye-level follow shot. The environment remains coherent without abrupt changes. Golden-hour warmth casts long reflections on the ground. She steps onto the board and pushes off repeatedly, accelerating along the sidewalk. Her jacket hem and hair flutter backward with speed. Background urban The camera tracks laterally from behind and slightly to the side, building momentum.

Shot 3 cuts hard into a close-up overhead extreme close-up. Focus is locked on the board and feet: the front foot angled slightly downward on the middle-front section, the back foot pressing the tail. Ground textures occasionally pass through the foreground, enhancing realism. Depth of field is shallow but foot positioning is highly visible. Warm natural light highlights the gritty texture of the grip tape. The board vibrates subtly due to speed and weight shifts. The camera closely follows with short-range tracking, tilting slightly to match balance changes, setting up for the jump.

Shot 4 cuts hard from the prior shot, switching to a medium-close low-angle upward shot. The background features street buildings and a small patch of open sky. Composition centers both the skater and board in frame. Backlighting creates a soft rim light around the sole and edge of the board. She forcefully stomps the tail to launch into a kickflip. During the full rotation, the angle of her shoe brushing the board is slightly off, causing the board to graze her front foot and land slightly skewed. She hastily taps the ground to stabilize but fails to land cleanly. Her brow furrows immediately, and she mutters with frustration “差一点”. The The crisp The camera quickly tilts up to follow the jump, then slightly down to capture the landing moment.

The subject stands on the left side of the frame, the board placed beside her feet. Background vehicles and pedestrians blur past without distracting. Warm light highlights sweat on her forehead and nose bridge. Shoulders relax, she repositions the board, and lightly touches her pants seam to adjust balance. The camera performs a minor pull-back and stops, creating a psychological buffer before re-engaging the action.

Shot 6 cuts hard back into a high-energy segment, using a wide-to-medium low-angle lateral follow shot. The foreground features an approaching small step, while the background continues the consistent urban street and warm-colored wall. Ground lines direct the viewer’s gaze toward the action point. Golden-hour light maintains visual unity. She re-accelerates, pushing harder. As she nears the step, her back foot firmly slams the tail, and her front foot swiftly flicks outward to scrape the board. The board rotates more cleanly and flatly. She tucks her knees mid-air, her jacket and hair lifted by speed. The board clears the step and reconnects with her feet. The camera performs a slight pull-back to keep her motion and smile fully within frame, ending on her elevated emotion under warm natural light.

Warm dawn light illuminates character edges from behind and side, while flickering torch embers add highlights in shadows. Bread swings short arms, cheese crouches into starting position. The camera slightly tilts down then slowly pushes in, building anticipation for the race start.

Shot 2 connects to previous shot via a hard cut triggered by the starting motion, medium eye-level tracking shot moving into the torch-lit corridor. Foreground occasionally sweeps past flickering flames and stone pillars; midground locks onto the bread runner sprinting ahead; background stone walls display magical runes flashing sequentially along the running path, creating strong depth. Strong leading lines from floor tiles and walls enhance perspective. Medium depth of field keeps both runner and wall runes sharp. Lighting remains warm torchlight mixed with soft dawn glow. Apple and cheese briefly appear behind, forming chase layers. Small accessories like cloth flaps and crumbs vibrate with speed. Camera tracks along the path with slight forward follow, enhancing speed sensation.

Shot 3 transitions from previous shot via a momentum-driven hard cut to a higher vantage point, overhead wide shot covering the complex route of suspension bridge connecting to spiral staircase. Foreground shows wooden planks and iron chains; midground features the cheese runner climbing strenuously; background reveals castle outer walls and lower courtyard bathed in golden dawn light. Lighting continues warm tone, with deeper contrast only in bridge shadows. Body shifts slightly forward, wooden planks tremble beneath feet, chains sway. Apple and bread flash past frame edges, creating pursuit pressure. Lute inserts denser, shorter plucks here; bellows hiss and bridge groans align precisely with climbing motions. Camera slowly descends from above the bridge and gently rotates along the stair arc, emphasizing vertical drop and physical exertion.

Shot 4 enters via a hard cut after corner obstruction, close-up eye-level shot transitioning to push-in at the armory’s exterior corner. Foreground shows hanging weapons and partially focused chains; midground features the apple runner suddenly cutting inside the corner and accelerating to overtake; background shows standing armor units trembling from airflow and vibration. Composition uses wall-floor intersection to direct focus toward the turn apex. Shallow depth of field emphasizes apple’s expression and motion. Warm torchlight creates dancing reflections on metal armor. Apple’s eyes are focused, leg stride increases, body leans sharply through the turn. Camera first moves short distance laterally, then abruptly pushes in on apple’s face, creating explosive overtaking impact.

Foreground shows wind-fluttering colored flags and finish banner; background features fully illuminated tower peak and distant city walls in dawn light. Flagpoles and eaves create upward leading lines, emphasizing victory. Deep depth of field ensures full visibility of finish environment. Lighting remains consistent warm gold; backlight outlines the runners’ edges. Brief suspension before landing causes flags, knots, and small debris to tremble in air. Cheers synchronize with characters’ open-mouthed shouting expressions. Camera quickly pushes in from low angle, then slightly tilts up, freezing at the peak moment of shared completion, forming a coherent and vibrant conclusion.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in from black. A wide overhead composition places the abandoned ring-shaped space station diagonally in the background, while a small exploration pod enters slowly from the lower left. The boy sits alone by the viewport, forming a foreground silhouette. The vastness of deep space contrasts sharply with the damaged station structure. Cold cosmic reflections sweep across metallic surfaces. Focus rests on the slowly approaching pod and the still figure of the boy. The camera moves forward extremely slowly with slight lateral drift to create a floating sensation. Near the end of the shot, a beeping alert for docking approaches.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut. A medium-level eye-level tracking shot follows the boy as he walks through an opening airlock. Floating dust and severed cables pass in the foreground, while the dimly lit corridor and flickering indicator lights form the background. Sparse cold light descends from overhead strip lights, and red warning lights occasionally sweep across walls. Each step produces a dull metallic echo. His arms slightly raise to maintain balance, and microgravity causes his clothing and backpack straps to float upward. The camera smoothly enters from outside the door and slightly pushes forward. The heavy impact of the airlock closing lands precisely in the middle of the shot.

Shot 3 transitions via a brief fade from the previous shot. A close-up low-angle shot focuses on the dormant spherical AI in the center of the control room. The boy stands slightly behind and to the right, creating a size contrast. The curved console surrounds the central subject. Shallow depth of field initially focuses on the dark, cracked surface of the sphere, then shifts to its core mirror as internal points of light activate one by one. Industrial cold lighting remains subdued. As the sphere awakens, a faint blue glow seeps outward from within. The boy leans forward cautiously, fingers hovering above the console without touching. The camera slowly pushes in and tilts up slightly, transforming the AI from inert to guiding presence. Emotion shifts from caution to curiosity.

Shot 4 cuts abruptly into dynamic action. A full shot side view captures the boy following the now-activated spherical AI through the observation gallery. The curved viewport frame appears in the foreground, while high-speed meteor showers rush past outside. Composition places the AI ahead and the boy behind, establishing clear guidance. When fragments strike the shield, concentric pale blue ripples spread across it. Interior cold light and exterior flashes alternate briefly. The boy instinctively raises a hand to shield his eyes before continuing forward. The camera tracks along the corridor with slight follow shake to enhance pressure.

Shot 5 transitions via a matching cut on the shield flash to the exterior. A medium-long shot from a low angle shows the boy exiting the maintenance hatch secured by a safety tether. The station's hull occupies the left foreground, while deep space and sparse stars fill the background. Cold backlight outlines the edges of his spacesuit. Distant red warning lights reflect repeatedly on his helmet glass. He grips the railing firmly, his body gently swaying under microgravity due to the tether. Then he extends a tool toward the break to begin repairs. His clothing, small accessories, and tether all lag slightly with motion. The camera moves from behind the hatch to the side front, completing a small arc to emphasize the scale of outer space.

Shot 6 cuts hard into the pre-climax sprint. A near-medium shot from above follows the boy leaping over floating debris inside the core shaft. The vertical shaft extends downward in the center, with weightless parts drifting in both foreground and background, creating depth. Focus remains locked on the energy chip in his hand and the target slot. Cold light radiates in rings from the shaft wall’s circular lights, with localized red warnings flickering at the edges. He first pushes off the wall to leap, avoiding a slowly rotating metal plate, then grabs a handrail with the other hand to stabilize himself before inserting the energy chip accurately into the main interface. The camera rapidly tilts down, then stops abruptly and pushes in, creating a sudden sense of falling speed.

Shot 7 transitions after a bright flash. A wide eye-level shot reveals the entire space station awakening from darkness. The ring structure lights up sequentially from partial to full. Control panels, navigation lights, and external beacons ignite like electric currents. In the foreground, the boy and AI stand at the end of a bridge, looking back. Their figures occupy only a small portion of the frame, fully releasing the grand scale of the reactivated station. Cool blue primary lighting stabilizes again, while red warning lights continue flashing but at decreasing frequency. The station transforms from derelict to orderly operation. The camera slowly pulls back and gently rises, revealing the full structure. Low-frequency electronic tones transition from tense to open, signaling clear emotional relief.

Shot 8 concludes with a fade-in/fade-out. A wide rear-tracking shot shows the boy piloting the exploration pod away from the starport. The spherical AI has transformed into a small companion drone flying steadily beside the pod. The port framework recedes in the foreground, while the reactivated station and deep space form the background. The departing pod is placed in the lower third of the frame, with the glowing ring of the starport forming a circular visual echo behind. The cool gray-blue tone remains consistent, but the awakened lights make the image more transparent. The boy glances back once through the viewport, and the AI drone slightly turns as if responding. The camera continues pulling back and slightly elevating, making both figures gradually shrink into tiny points of light in the starfield. All alarms have completely faded. Only calm electronic echoes remain, along with a single gentle departure confirmation tone, ending the adventure quietly and hopefully.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide overhead perspective from high altitude, diagonally looking down at the trenches outside the city. Trenches and copper pipe cover form strong leading lines extending toward the steampunk mechanical city. Foreground includes swirling sand and partially obscured rusted gears; background features steam-shrouded walls and slowly rotating massive mechanical structures. Deep depth of field fully establishes battlefield layers. Warm evening light comes from the rear-side, casting dark golden reflections on copper surfaces. Three armored pandas crouch behind copper pipe cover, bodies low, eyes fixed toward the city gate. Armor edges and flags flutter in the wind, steam intermittently erupting. The camera slowly descends and slightly advances toward the trench, setting up focus on the commander in the next shot.

Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, switching to a medium-close eye-level slightly low-angle push-in. Composition centers on the commanding panda, positioned slightly left of center. Foreground cover edge is blurred; background features white-steam-emitting brass pipes and flickering furnace flames. Shallow depth of field emphasizes tactical movements. Side lighting slices across its armor texture and facial fur, with warm copper tones mixed with faint gray-white highlights from scattered steam. It raises its claw tip and quickly draws bridges and attack routes on a metal tactical map. As the claw moves, fine dust and glints are stirred up. Two other pandas remain low and alert in the background. After a smooth push-in, the camera slightly shifts right, reinforcing the decisiveness after the order.

Shot 3 continues with a hard cut, transitioning to a full-shot tracking shot from a low side-rear angle, following the squad as they burst from cover and cross the steam-pipe bridge. The bridge surface consists of parallel copper pipes and riveted planks. Foreground elements rapidly pass by—steam valves and hanging chains—while background reveals a wall breach and rotating gear towers. Spatial direction strictly matches the route drawn in the previous shot’s tactical map. Lighting remains dominated by warm dusk light and furnace reflections. Steam churns beneath the bridge, forming a flowing mist layer. The panda squad runs low, armor clanking softly during movement. A few sparks graze the armor edges, briefly trailing bright streaks. A sudden pressure release from a side vent sends white steam sweeping past the characters’ bodies. Cloaks and armor plates flutter with momentum. The camera uses fast pan with slight handheld shake to convey speed. Ambient No additional

Shot 4 uses a hard cut matched to action, cutting to a close-up low-angle shot at the bridge exit. Focus locks onto the lead panda leaping from the trench edge into backlight. Foreground includes kicked-up gravel and swirling steam. Background features a golden sunset dimmed by smoke and faintly burning furnaces. The character’s silhouette is outlined in bright light, armor seams and fur tips glowing with vibrant gold-red. Its claws extend forward, body airborne, with a brief pause before landing enhancing power. The camera first tilts up slightly, then surges forward, creating explosive momentum.

Shot 5 cuts hard from the previous shot and transitions to a wide pull-out for closure, shooting from above the gear plaza and pulling back diagonally. The plaza floor consists of circular gear tracks, copper bricks, and steam manholes. A central flag tower rises tall, surrounded by operating mechanical arms and rotating gears. Foreground shows the charging panda squad; background reveals the city outline illuminated by sunset and furnace fire, smoke curling in golden-red light. The lead panda reaches the base of the flag tower first. Others quickly disperse, secure surrounding paths, and collectively seize the high control point. The flag unfurls dramatically in the strong wind. Action flows naturally from ground sprint to vertical capture. Sparks on armor gradually fade, while steam still intermittently bursts from base vents. Metal components on the plaza continue vibrating from the charge’s momentum. Emotion shifts from tension to triumphant victory. The camera continuously pulls back and slightly elevates, encompassing the panda squad, flag tower, gear plaza, and the entire steampunk city bathed in twilight, concluding with a grand scene of conquest.

prompts: Shot 1 opens directly with a wide overhead view. The composition uses vertical lines formed by the bus stop pillars, foreground showing wind-blown dust and scattered metal parts, midground featuring a temporary vanity made of a cracked mirror and rusted metal box, and background including faded signage and tilted benches. A soft misty cool blue-gray watercolor wash gives the space a desolate yet gentle feel. The smiling toast sits upright before the vanity, tools neatly laid out: small brush, cotton pad, base cream container, silver-gray eyeliner pencil, and glitter container clearly visible. Dust occasionally drifts across the mirror's edge, and the paper-like outline is gently highlighted by cold light. The camera slowly moves forward slightly from above with a slight downward tilt, establishing the environment and drawing visual focus toward the vanity.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a close-up eye-level view. Focus locks onto the area around the left eye, with the blurred edge of the cracked mirror in the foreground forming a framing device. Eye texture and tiny sand particles are clearly visible in shallow depth of field. The scene remains within the same bus stop, with cold daylight coming from the side-rear, reflecting softly off the inner surface of the metal box, illuminating the eye area without glare. A hand holding a cotton pad gently wipes away debris around the left eye, then uses fingertips to thinly spread base cream. The sequence is clear: after wiping, debris reduces and the surface becomes smooth, leaving a subtly moist, even texture. Corresponding Chinese The camera stays mostly stable, with only a very slight push-in to emphasize tutorial details and hand precision.

Shot 3 connects via action-matched editing, smoothly transitioning from the base cream pressing gesture into a close-up eye-level view with a slight upward angle. Rusty bus window frames in the background are softened into gentle color blocks. The cool blue-gray palette continues, with the upper eyelid appearing more translucent due to light refraction. After dipping the small brush in icy blue eyeshadow, it lightly sweeps from the inner corner toward the center, then gently extends toward the outer corner, gradually building color intensity. As pigment adheres, the eyelid surface transitions from matte base cream to a fine, frosty cool-toned layer. The camera performs a slow push-in, slightly following the brush movement to ensure clear visibility of bristle contact and color application path.

Shot 4 transitions via a subtle dissolve from the previous shot, entering an extreme close-up eye-level view. The frame almost entirely shows the left eye, outer corner, and handheld tools. The cracked mirror’s fracture patterns create fragmented highlights along the edges, enhancing the wasteland feel without distracting from readability. Lighting remains dominated by cold daylight and faint artificial cold light, with glitter producing sharper silver-white reflections at the outer corner. The eye makeup evolves from flat coloring into a layered structure, with texture shifting from soft matte to localized sparkle.

Shot 5 cuts sharply from the previous shot and pulls back to a medium-close eye-level view. Composition centers the smiling toast, with the cracked mirror in the foreground reflecting the completed makeup on the left side, while the untouched right side retains its original state, creating a natural before-and-after contrast. The background re-establishes the abandoned bus stop and rising dust, completing the narrative loop. Cold light clearly reveals the icy blue and silver-gray layers of the single-eye makeup, with glitter flashing briefly only during blinking, preserving the overall reserved tone. The subject slightly turns head, pauses momentarily to display the difference between sides, then gently blinks the completed eye, finally offering a gentle smile. The before-and-after contrast is clear and definitive, concluding the tutorial with a result showcase. The final Chinese The camera slowly pulls back and slightly pans right, keeping both the mirrored reflection and real front-facing image in frame, clearly ending the entire lesson.

An elderly male stands beside the table, firmly securing the work area and disconnecting power. The camera performs a slight push-in, helping viewers quickly grasp the safety starting point.

The scene transitions. Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a close-up eye-level view focusing on the stone table surface. Solder wire spool, flux bottle, and tweezers are arranged diagonally, with the rune circuit board blurred in the background as a guide. Firelight remains the key light, with blue rune reflections on metallic edges. The instructor's fingers point to each tool in turn; objects emit subtle pixel shimmer when touched. Chinese voiceover simultaneously names their functions, maintaining a composed tone. The camera performs a short lateral slide, following the hand movement from left to right to complete the inventory.

The scene transitions. Shot 3 transitions via hard cut to an extreme close-up from a slightly angled overhead perspective. Focus centers on the iron tip and damp cleaning sponge. Foreground shows the glowing iron tip, background softly blurred to retain flux bottle and stone texture. Warm light creates stable highlights on metal surfaces. The instructor first cleans the iron tip, then gently touches solder to the tip to form an even thin layer. Chinese The camera makes a slight tilt-down motion, pressing details more fully into frame.

The scene transitions. Shot 4 continues with a hard cut to a medium-close overhead view using a tutorial-style top-down composition. Stone table edge forms a stable frame, hands centered in the image, wire, wire stripper, and circuit board pads clearly arranged front-to-back. Key light still comes from upper-right warm fire bowl, fill light from left-side blue rune lamp. The instructor first strips the wire to expose neat metal strands, then quickly pre-tins the pad with the iron. Both wire end and pad surface show uniform shiny thin solder layers. Chinese The camera remains stable, only making a minimal push-in to enhance step readability.

The scene transitions. Shot 5 cuts via hard cut to a close-up eye-level view. Composition places the rune circuit board in the lower half of the frame, foreground slightly blurred with a short piece of solder wire, midground clearly showing hole positions, background revealing the instructor’s chest leather apron and flickering firelight. A resistor and an LED are picked up one by one, oriented correctly, and inserted into board holes. The moment component leads pass through holes aligns clearly with pixelated copper traces on the board. Chinese The camera performs a slow lateral follow, ensuring finger, component, and hole relationships remain clear.

The scene transitions. Shot 6 cuts via hard cut to an extreme close-up at a slightly upward-angled eye-level view. Pad and component lead occupy the center of frame, shallow depth of field blurring the workshop background into soft pixel blocks. Iron tip enters from the right side, contacting both pad and lead simultaneously. Then solder is fed from the left. Upon heating, solder flows, spreads, and contracts into a full, conical joint. This material transformation is the focal point of this shot. The instructor emphasizes “烙铁同时碰焊盘和引脚”, with sentence timing perfectly aligned to the moment the iron touches. The camera performs a very short push-in, enhancing the credibility of the joint formation detail.

The scene transitions. Shot 7 connects via hard cut to a medium eye-level shot beginning a dolly move. Composition smoothly shifts from one side of the board to the other. Foreground occasionally sweeps past tweezers and snips, adding speed layering. Midground continuously locks onto the soldering area. Warm firelight maintains table clarity, blue fill light outlines edges. The instructor completes the other side using the same method, then cleanly clips excess leads with snips. Metal fragments bounce to the edge of the stone table. Movements are fluid and controlled. Chinese voiceover briefly supplements the trimming step.

The scene transitions. Shot 8 cuts via hard cut to an extreme close-up overhead view. Centered are several completed joints. Foreground shows magnifier frame edge, background displays faint rune patterns. Lighting remains consistent, with slightly enhanced highlight reflection on joint surfaces. The instructor gently prods components with tweezers to confirm stability, then checks each joint for fullness, roundness, absence of cold solder or bridging. Joint surfaces display clear light-dark block changes in pixel art style. Chinese Camera nearly static, only making a tiny zoom-in to enhance inspection feel.

The scene transitions. Shot 9 connects via a gentle fade-in/fade-out transition, shifting to a close-up eye-level view with rapid push-in. The rune circuit board at the center of the stone table becomes the main subject again. Foreground shows power switch, background reveals the elderly male’s facial outline with satisfied smile. Warm firelight illuminates his wrinkles, cool blue rune light gradually lights up the board in grid pattern. After he turns on the power, runes glow steadily rather than flicker, component operation status clearly visible. In the final half-second, the camera freezes between the glowing circuit board and his smile, forming a complete, coherent, executable tutorial ending.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a direct cut, wide eye-level shot, using floor directional lines to guide the viewer’s gaze toward the right-side first aid training corner. Blurred passengers pass in the foreground while the background clearly shows the training mat, dummy, AED trainer, and signage. The environment is clean and bright, illuminated evenly by cool white lights. An elderly male stands at the center of the training area facing the camera, ready to demonstrate. The camera slowly pushes forward to establish the space.

Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, medium high-angle composition, focusing on the safe zone between the elderly male and the ground dummy. The foreground includes the edge of the training mat, and the background retains station signage. He first scans the surroundings, confirming no incoming trains or scattered obstacles, then signals that the area is safe before approaching the dummy. Lighting remains steady and natural. Chinese The camera performs a slight downward tilt to emphasize the sequence of inspection actions.

Shot 3 connects via a match-on-action hard cut to the previous shot, close-up eye-level, framing focused on the dummy’s shoulder and the demonstrator’s upper body. Shallow depth of field slightly blurs the background concourse. He kneels on one knee, taps the shoulder, and leans forward to call out. His facial expression remains composed, hand movements clear and controlled. Cool white light creates soft contrast on his face and back of hands. Chinese The camera makes a very short push-in to highlight the key action.

Shot 4 transitions with a slight dissolve into a medium-close high-angle shot. The demonstrator places one hand on the forehead and observes chest rise/fall, then lifts his head to call for help and signal retrieval of the AED trainer. Lighting remains even, with neutral visuals avoiding exaggeration.

Shot 5 cuts hard from the previous shot, full shot eye-level, framing the entire training mat. The dummy is centered, and the elderly male adjusts its position on the left side of the frame. Using both hands, he controls the shoulders and torso to properly place the dummy in a supine position, moving steadily without dragging. The setting remains the same training corner, with consistent floor texture and equipment placement. The Chinese The camera performs a brief lateral follow move to ensure the repositioning process is fully visible.

Shot 6 cuts via action match to a close-up high-angle shot, focusing on the dummy’s chest and the demonstrator’s overlapping hands. No distracting elements in the foreground; the background is compressed into softly blurred training mat texture. He quickly and accurately locates the compression point along the sternum, then firmly places the heel of his palm. Overhead cool white light sharply defines finger contours and chest movement. Chinese The camera remains nearly static, with only a subtle push-in to make hand positioning unmistakable.

Faint station lighting in the background enhances realism. Slight fabric movement follows body motion, making arm exertion and recoil clearly visible. Lighting remains uniform and subdued. Chinese The camera uses micro-follow zooming to maintain force sense and teaching clarity.

Shot 8 transitions with fade-in/fade-out to a medium-close side-high-angle shot, framing head, jaw, and chest in one frame. Focus lies on hand movement across forehead and chin. Lighting remains dominated by overhead concourse light, with soft facial shadows. Chinese The camera slides briefly along the head-shoulder axis to clarify action layers.

Shot 9 cuts hard to an adjacent choking demonstration area on the concourse side, medium eye-level. Foreground features upright training mannequin and safety signage; background still shows subway concourse directional signs. Environment transition is logical and smooth. Overall neutral tone and lighting remain consistent. Piano Chinese The camera performs a small lateral shift to complete the area transition.

Shot 10 cuts via action match from the previous shot, close-up rear eye-level, focusing on the demonstrator’s hands and the mannequin’s abdomen. Foreground shows his stable forearm; background softly blurred to station wall. He wraps arms around the mannequin from behind, precisely locates two fingers above the navel, clenches fist, inserts it, and demonstrates Heimlich maneuver inward and upward. Body force path is clear, motion fluid but not exaggerated. Overhead light creates distinct layers on hands and clothing folds. Chinese The camera slightly pushes in to emphasize hand placement and direction of force.

Shot 11 fades in from the previous shot, medium-wide eye-level, returning to the full training area. Foreground shows neatly stored AED trainer and training mat. Focus rests on the elderly male facing the camera in summary pose. Background concourse remains stably operational, lighting unchanged. Chinese The camera slowly pulls back, ending the entire process with a calm, clear instructional finish.

Shot 3 connects via a match-on-action cut to the ridge path, using a medium side-angle shot. The subject is positioned slightly left of center, with continuous mountain lines extending into the right rear, creating clear depth. Her steps are slow and steady, playing uninterrupted. The camera follows her laterally at the same direction, occasionally lifting slightly to emphasize spatial progression from forest to higher elevation.

Shot 4 transitions via a fade-in emotional cut to the stone platform at the summit, using a wide-to-medium-long shot composition with a slightly upward eye-level angle. The stone platform is centered as a stable focal point. Overall lighting remains soft and natural, with only faint highlights on the subject’s silhouette and strings. After completing the final gentle pluck, her fingers pause halfway on the strings. In the The camera continues to slowly pull back, gradually integrating the person, platform, and cloud sea into a complete summit scene, ultimately resting on a serene and ethereal conclusion.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide-angle eye-level shot with a slight downward angle. Depth of field clearly establishes the Eastern mythological fairyland setting. A young woman carrying a guitar steps onto the wooden platform from the edge of the mist, her sleeves gently swaying with each step. Soft light evenly illuminates her clothing and guitar, while only a faint backlight outlines her silhouette in the distance. The camera slowly pushes in, naturally establishing her entrance and the opening atmosphere.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut, transitioning to a close-up at eye level, focusing on the moment her left hand presses the frets and right hand lightly strums the strings. The neck extends diagonally from the bottom-left to top-right corner. In the background, the jade bridge's end is partially obscured by mist. The environment remains consistent within the same stage space, progressing forward. Soft lighting continues to highlight the metallic strings and fingertip texture. The camera makes a small push along the neck direction, emphasizing control and rhythmic establishment at the start of the performance.

Shot 3 transitions via match-on-action editing into a close-up at eye level. Shallow depth of field blurs the background cloud bridge and stone platform, keeping only fingertips, pick, and strings as visual focus. Composition places fingers slightly right of center for clear visibility of sliding paths and subtle vibrations as the pick sweeps across the strings. Under soft light, string reflections appear fragmented, while minimal backlight creates gentle highlights on knuckle edges. After completing a smooth slide, the young woman executes two rapid plucks.

Shot 4 transitions via a smooth pan to a medium side-angle shot, extending the scene naturally to a waterside corridor connected to the same fairyland stage. The railing and water reflection form clear leading lines. The subject occupies the left third of the frame, with slow-moving mist and bridge shadows in the background. The overall tone remains neutral with soft lighting. Her skirt and long sleeves create more pronounced arcs due to motion. Emotion shifts from ethereal to a more distinct sense of momentum.

Shot 5 cuts sharply into a medium-wide side-backlight shot, advancing the scene to the edge of a platform near a waterfall. Mist in the background forms bright layers, outlining the subject and guitar with subtle backlight. Soft lighting still supports facial and hand details. Her performance reaches its climax, with rapid arpeggios and broad strums unfolding continuously.

Shot 6 connects via a whip pan to an overhead close-up, locking onto the guitar body, hands, and swirling sleeves from above. Wood grain on the platform is clearly visible. Composition radiates outward, with the guitar at the center and sleeves forming a rotating visual effect around it. Soft lighting renders fabric layers gently, while a faint backlight enhances action contours at the edges. During continuous strumming, she performs a light turn, causing her sleeves to flare and the wooden platform to vibrate slightly.

Shot 7 cuts sharply and quickly pulls back into a wide-angle low-angle shot, expanding the space to include floating stone steps and layered cloud seas atop a mountain peak. The subject stands on the foreground platform, with distant spectators appearing as small silhouettes scattered across the steps and bridgeheads. Foreground, midground, and background layers are clearly defined. Lighting remains consistent, with backlight slightly enhanced to strengthen the edge presence. The camera retreats while subtly tilting upward, elevating the stage into a broader mythic landscape.

Shot 8 connects gently via a fade-in/fade-out transition to a close-up at eye level. The mountain-top platform contracts back into an intimate space between the subject and her guitar. Background clouds and distant mountains are compressed into a soft shallow depth of field. Composition centers the face and guitar headstock visually. Soft lighting returns as dominant, with minimal backlight preserving only hair tips and shoulder lines. After completing the final downward strum, she briefly freezes her motion. The string resonance clearly lingers in the air. The camera makes an extremely slight push-in at the final moment before stopping, cleanly landing the farewell expression and terminal note.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide overhead view to establish the full orbital lab. Curved walls and floating instruments form clear leading lines. In the foreground, a data board floats slowly; in the midground, a fish gently sways its tail fin in microgravity; in the background, a transparent crystallization chamber is fixed at the center of the lab, with slow-moving nebulae visible through the viewport. Under cool dominant lighting, metallic surfaces reflect high-saturation glints. The fish explores around the chamber, adjusting position, conveying quiet tension before the experiment begins. Chinese The camera slowly pushes in from above with a slight downward tilt.

Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, focusing on a close-up eye-level view of the transparent operation area. Shallow depth of field blurs the background wall, keeping only the seed container and the fish's precise movements in focus. A transparent tube, supersaturated solution syringe, and seed chamber form a clean triangular composition. Stable cool light from internal instruments illuminates the scene, with fine highlights outlining the edge of the seed container. The fish stabilizes its body with slight movements and slowly injects the supersaturated solution into the container. In microgravity, the liquid forms a smooth, floating stream that is precisely guided into the chamber. The camera performs a small lateral pan and gently pushes in to highlight the injection interface.

Shot 3 transitions via match cut to a macro time-lapse close-up. The shot is a tight eye-level view near the inner wall of the transparent crystallization chamber. Small bubbles occasionally drift across the foreground. The midground shows the seed surface, while the background features dimmed lab light strips. Within the unified cool blue tone, the crystal edges begin to refract high-saturation iridescent highlights. The frame emphasizes the continuous transformation: from clear solution to tiny nuclei, then to uniformly radiating crystal branches. The structure evolves from points and lines into layered, branching 3D formations. The camera remains mostly stable, with only minimal push-in to enhance growth details.

Shot 4 fades into a medium follow shot, using a slightly upward eye-level angle to convey spatial depth. The transparent crystallization chamber is centered, with the fish circling it, forming a circular motion path. Floating record cards occasionally pass in the foreground. The midground shows the continuously expanding crystal branches, while the background features moving nebula light bands outside the viewport. Lighting remains dominated by soft internal lights and crystal-reflected highlights. The fish adjusts its swimming speed while observing, and the crystal branches continue to extend outward, becoming sharper in outline. The camera smoothly pans around the fish’s trajectory with slight pitch adjustments.

Shot 5 cuts hard from the previous shot, followed by a brief pause. It uses a wide static eye-level composition. The mature crystal chamber is positioned at the golden ratio point. In the foreground, a softly blurred control panel light appears. The midground features a complete, clearly layered transparent mature crystal. In the background, through the viewport, a high-saturation nebula slowly expands, framing the experimental result against the cosmic backdrop. Lighting remains clear and cool, creating delicate bright edges on the crystal. The fish hovers quietly on one side, no longer operating. The image clearly conveys the stable state of completed experimentation. The camera performs a very slight pull-out, placing the crystal, fish, and nebula into a complete closing composition.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in from black, a wide overhead shot of the medieval castle tower at night. Foreground features blurred stone eaves and vines, background shows deep blue sky and thin clouds. Focus is on the gently flickering orange-red light from a high window in the tower. Low-saturation watercolor edges make the stone texture appear softly diffused like paper in a picture book. Cold night surrounds the warm glow. The camera slowly pushes forward along the tower wall, drawing viewers toward the glowing window.

Shot 2 hard cuts from previous shot to interior of the castle, a full shot eye-level capturing a boy walking through a narrow corridor toward the alchemy table. Arched stone columns frame both sides, forming leading lines. Old bricks on the floor reflect candlelight. Occasionally, a wall sconce passes through foreground, creating soft obstruction. Focus remains steady on the small bottle he holds and his steps. Warm candlelight remains dominant, while faint cold blue reflections are visible from the far end of the lab. The camera performs smooth lateral tracking, conveying spatial continuity from corridor to alchemy room.

Shot 3 transitions from previous shot with brief fade to close-up overhead view focusing on the alchemy table surface. On the wooden table are several small bottles, salt powders, metal spoons, and a small furnace. Foreground shows blurred edge of a half-open wooden box. Focus shifts slowly from labeled bottle tops to the boy’s fingers as he arranges powder in neat piles. Powder particles retain dry, fine texture even under watercolor rendering. The furnace is not yet lit. Candlelight from side-rear highlights subtle surface undulations. The camera uses extremely slow overhead drift and slight focus shift to present the precise sequence of preparation.

Shot 4 hard cuts from previous shot to close-up eye-level shot. The furnace opening occupies center-lower frame. The boy brings an ignition tool near the wick. Foreground shows a small pile of unused powder blurred into pale patches. The first orange flame leaps up instantly upon contact, sparks briefly scatter then quickly retract. Warm light immediately overwhelms the dim surroundings, illuminating his fingertips and furnace rim. The camera makes a brief push-in, locking onto the instant the flame forms.

Shot 5 transitions from previous shot via action match to macro close-up overhead view. The boy gently sprinkles the first type of powder into the orange flame. Shallow depth of field makes the powder’s trajectory into the flame the absolute focal point. Originally orange flame rapidly turns green and curls upward. Color change starts from base and spreads to tip. Warm candlelight still casts soft shadows in background.

Shot 6 hard cuts from previous shot to close-up eye-level shot. Another small spoon delivers copper salt to the edge of the small furnace. Foreground shows blurred blue-gray outline of a glass bottle. Focus is on the slender flame tongue. New flame shows colder blue at root and extends higher and thinner, gently swaying in air currents. Flame edges are transparent, center brighter, forming a clear and continuous experimental progression from previous green flame. Environment remains dual illumination of candlelight and colored flames. Gentle glass and metal clinks interject. Camera performs very controlled lateral micro-move, making blue flame appear to glide quietly within frame.

Shot 7 transitions from previous shot with soft fade to medium overhead view. Multiple small bottles are neatly arranged on wooden table. Flame tongues in different furnaces vary in height. Orange, green, and blue flames create layered rhythmic progression on same surface. Foreground shows unopened bottle stopper. Background features softly blurred stone wall and pages. Focus centers on silhouette of staggered flame tips. Overhead composition makes experimental order immediately clear. Candlelight warms wood grain. Colored flames cast alternating warm and cool shadows on table. Camera performs slow overhead drift, scanning left to right across entire row of flames, ensuring each form is fully visible.

Shot 8 hard cuts from previous shot to close-up eye-level slightly overhead angle. Boy lifts glass cover from top of frame and slowly lowers it over one flame. Foreground shows reflection on transparent glass edge. Background is blurred bookshelf and stone wall. Focus locks on flame shape changing within cover. Originally scattered flame gradually becomes narrower, straighter, and more stable under cover. Blue-green light spots shimmer on glass surface. Emotion here slightly pauses. Camera performs slight downward tilt and push-in, emphasizing observation action and subtle changes in constrained flame.

Frame focuses on boy’s face. He slightly raises head, watching flame color inside glass cover. Blue, green, and red reflections successively illuminate his cheeks, eyelashes, and eyes. Occasional out-of-focus flame tongue passes through foreground, naturally linking character and experimental result. Background alchemy room recedes into soft color blocks. Candlelight maintains warm base tone on skin. Colored flames leave dreamy, controlled cool highlights on face.

Shot 10 transitions from previous shot with fade-in/fade-out to wide full shot eye-level with slight pull-back. Entire alchemy room appears like a quiet page from a picture book. Stone walls, candle stands, wooden tables, medicine bottles, books, and several still-gently-flickering colored flames are fully framed. Composition centers alchemy table slightly forward, with night outside tower window in distant background. A stationary glass cover in foreground echoes earlier scene. Focus expands gradually from person and flames to entire room, restoring calmness. Warm candlelight and cool flame light continue to unify the scene. Camera slowly pulls back and slightly elevates, freezing the entire lab in low-saturation watercolor texture as a tranquil and mysterious conclusion.

prompts: The boy wears a simple lab apron, steps light and steady.

Shot 2: hard cut to close-up, side view, tracking pan — the camera glides along the edge of the stone table, foreground sweeping past brass supports and glass narrow-neck bottles, focus on the boy’s extended hand and the small flame device beneath the glass vessel beside the table. Interior lighting continues the mix of soft window light and warm fire glow. He touches the ignition rod to the flame port; the small flame ignites steadily from dim to bright, warm reflection appears on the bottom of the glass. The tracking pan precisely follows the hand motion. The brass bellows

Shot 3: match-cut transition to extreme close-up, overhead — desktop composition is orderly, spiral glass tube centered, flanked by containers of blue and gold liquids. Shallow depth of field blurs background parchment and brass measuring tools. The boy slowly pours both liquids into the same flask; blue and gold liquids slide down the spiral tube wall, layers accumulate in the flask, tiny bubbles rise along the liquid column. The camera maintains slight downward pressure to emphasize material change.

Shot 4: hard cut to extreme close-up, eye-level, dolly in — the flask nearly fills the frame, foreground glass edge refracts cold color patches from the stained glass, focus tightly locked on the liquid inside. Light remains soft but flame reflection warms the base. The mixed liquid initially stays indigo, then a jade-green diffusion band emerges in the center, spreading like ink slowly bleeding on paper. The dolly-in makes the color shift clearer from overall to local texture. The harpsichord adds a brighter broken chord at the color transition point, liquid flow

Shot 5: brief dissolve to close-up, low angle — camera looks up from the edge of the stone table, brass valve in the foreground, the boy’s hand and face in the same focal plane. The low angle creates an upward action chain of valve, flask, and his focused expression. Background is soft light from high stained glass. He slowly turns the brass valve; Fine mist first rises in the flask, then gathers on the inner walls and gradually solidifies into translucent jelly-like substance. The camera slightly follows the hand in an arc-shaped movement.

Shot 6: hard cut to extreme close-up, overhead — perspective returns to objective documentation. Flask opening, gel surface, and tiny bubbles form main visual focus. Foreground is a blurred measuring spoon, background blurred stone table texture. Gel has stabilized, color slowly fading from jade green edges to amber, internal translucent layers and slowly moving thread-like patterns visible. Camera sinks extremely slightly closer, emphasizing surface viscosity and color gradation. Harpsichord slows, gear stirrer

Shot 7: hard cut to medium shot, eye-level, tracking pan — camera slides from the side of the flask to the boy’s face, using parallel composition of person and table. Foreground is the finished container, background softly blurred bookshelf and hanging tools. Soft window light illuminates his eyes and slightly raised lips.

Shot 8: soft fade cut to close-up, low angle, pull out — the boy carries the finished product to the stained glass window. Initial focus is on the edge texture of the translucent gel in the container, then as the camera pulls back, his upper body and the window are gradually included. Low angle outlines the container sharply against window light. Amber gel shows fine phase transition textures and translucent layers, refracting gentle glow like thin honey. He gently rotates the container to observe changes from different angles. Pull-out expands spatial relationship. Bellows

Shot 9: hard cut to wide shot, overhead, slow pull out — entire alchemy lab returns to tranquility. Stone table, glassware, brass pipes, valves, and high windows form clear order in overhead composition. Boy sits back at the desk, places the finished product aside, writes down experimental results on parchment with the other hand. Fine scratching Window light and residual fire maintain consistent lighting tone. Camera slowly pulls back, shrinking the figure into quiet space.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, showing a wide overhead view of the stone pavilion on cloud platform and surrounding misty mountains. Stone railings, eaves, and distant misty bridge form layered leading lines. In the foreground, gauze and drooping branches flutter gently in the wind. In the midground, an elderly man with white beard stands before a table. The background features a hazy lotus pond and faint green mountain silhouettes. Soft light descends from above, focusing on the central bronze mirror and jade cup on the pavilion. The The camera performs a very slow downward tilt followed by a slight push-in, establishing spatial relationships between the mythical environment and experimental apparatus.

Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, transitioning to a medium eye-level shot that slowly pushes in. The composition uses the table as a horizontal axis. The elder’s hands, one in front and one behind, steadily manipulate the ancient bronze mirror and water-filled jade cup. Shallow depth of field blurs the misty background, focusing on the moment sunlight reflected from the mirror enters the cup. The water surface starts still, then develops small ripples, creating a soft, bright bent trajectory of refracted light in the air. A flickering highlight appears on bamboo scrolls and jade objects beside the table. The guqin continues playing; the wooden wheel The camera moves smoothly along the table axis, clearly showing the process of light entering the vessel.

Shot 3 cuts hard into a close-up eye-level shot, tightly framing the edge of the prism and the bronze mirror surface. The foreground shows a slightly bluish crystal facet, while the background is a blurred red wall. Focus shifts with the mirror’s angle to the dancing reflection spots on the wall. Under side lighting, fine oxidation textures on the mirror, prism edges, and the transformation of light spots—from scattered to concentrated and then lightly jumping—are meticulously recorded. The watercolor brushstroke texture makes highlights appear softly diffused like paint.

Shot 4 transitions from the previous shot via a soft dissolve, shifting to a close-up overhead view of the table. The jade cup, bronze mirror, prism, and the elder’s hands form a stable diagonal composition. Focus gradually shifts from fingers to the flowing caustic patterns on the tabletop. As the elder slowly rotates the mirror, ripples spread across the water in the cup, and caustic patterns glide over the wooden surface, curled bamboo scrolls, and blue-green jade paperweight like fish scales. The shape of the bright spots evolves from fragmented dots to sheet-like streaks, then re-converges. Lighting remains consistently natural daylight with side illumination. The camera performs a slight overhead circular pan and minor downward tilt, making the dynamic light patterns the absolute focal point.
Shot 5 cuts abruptly to a close-up, eye-level view, framing the elder's upper body and the object in his hands.

Shot 6 follows seamlessly with a tracking shot, following a chain of moving light spots away from the table. It first passes the edge of the pavilion, then glides over the railing of the misty bridge, finally landing on the lotus pond surface. The shot naturally transitions from medium to long-medium, maintaining a level perspective slightly low, forming rich depth with bridge shadows, railings, and water ripples as leading lines. Focus continuously tracks how the light spot changes across different materials: sharp and defined on the stone railing, softened in the mist beneath the bridge, brief flashes on lotus leaves, and stretched into long strips by water ripples. Bridge shadows and water patterns reflect each other, creating a continuous and gentle visual echo. The camera smoothly tracks laterally with a slight downward tilt, ensuring the full path of light diffusion remains coherent.

Shot 7 connects to the previous shot through a fade-in/fade-out spatial expansion, ultimately pulling back to a wide-angle elevated but nearly level view. The pavilion, misty bridge, lotus pond, distant mountains, and clouds all enter the frame. Soft foreground mist and flowering branches create a gentle framing. In the midground, the elder remains standing calmly at the pavilion. In the background, the entire paradise is progressively illuminated by flowing caustic spots. Red walls, bridge surfaces, pond water, and mist all display fine, dynamic light patterns. Focus gradually shifts from the character to the entire space being lit. The light is not harsh but warm and luminous, filtered through water and mist. The final guqin note gently fades, coinciding with the last light spot dissolving into the mist. The camera continues to pull back smoothly with a slight upward tilt, concluding the optical demonstration in serene and ethereal silence.

prompts: Shot 1 opens directly with a wide, eye-level shot, the camera dollying along the edge of the coastal mangrove forest. In the foreground, fluorescent leaves flutter gently in the sea breeze; in the midground, an elephant wearing glowing goggles; in the background, the intertidal zone, rocks, and shallow water reflections are bathed in both sunset and neon glow. Lighting continues with warm orange sunset outlining the subject's silhouette, while magenta neon from the side-rear highlights the edges of the apparatus and the glowing details of the goggles. On screen, the elephant steadily sets up the transparent droplet apparatus, adjusting the nozzle alignment with the glowing measuring cup below.

Shot 2 follows the previous shot with a hard cut, transitioning to a close-up, low-angle shot. The camera moves slightly forward from beneath the nozzle, shallow depth of field locking focus tightly on the point where the amber high-viscosity liquid meets the nozzle. Background neon blocks of the mangrove forest blur into soft bokeh. Compositionally, the thin liquid thread runs vertically through the center of the frame, with the nozzle positioned at the upper golden ratio point, naturally guiding the viewer’s gaze toward the thinnest part of the deformation. Lighting remains dominated by warm orange and magenta, with slow-moving highlights reflecting off the liquid surface, emphasizing the thick, sticky texture of the high-viscosity material. The frame captures the full process: the liquid slowly bulging from the nozzle, being pulled into a long thread by gravity, and gradually forming a fuller droplet at the bottom. Physical state changes are continuously visible, with the stretching process clearly slow, progressively thinning but not easily breaking. The faint pulling The camera push-in is controlled, enhancing the sense of microscopic observation.

Shot 3 transitions from the previous shot with a slight fade-in continuous cut, switching to a medium shot, high angle. The camera slowly pulls back from above the measuring cup. Foreground shows the edge and scale markings of the glowing cup; midground features the droplet finally detaching from the thread and falling into the cup; background gradually reveals rocks, mudflats, and mangroves illuminated by warm neon, recontextualizing the experimental result within the environment. Composition centers on the measuring cup, with the moment the droplet hits creating small ripples that spread outward, combining with the cup’s scale markings and surrounding neon reflections to form layered expanding visual focus. Lighting remains consistent, with the glowing liquid surface inside the cup displaying soft luminous layers under warm orange sunset, while magenta fill light gently sweeps across the ripple edges. Visually, the droplet completes detachment and falls into the cup, creating small but clear ripples on the surface. The apparatus remains suspended above, completing a full experimental loop from setup, stretching, to drop-in. The elephant stands aside, observing the result and slightly lifting its trunk in a summarizing gesture. The camera pulls back to conclude the film, stabilizing the final second with a unified blend of experimental conclusion, natural scenery, and cyberpunk aesthetic.

Shallow depth of field keeps both the character and device sharp while slightly blurring the background crowd. Soft light evenly fills the hall, with gentle reflections on glass surfaces but no glare. the second half lands precisely on the moment his lips curl upward and his finger freezes.

Shot 2 connects to the previous shot via a hard cut, transitioning to a close-up side angle. The camera quickly pans near one side of the protective shield, shifting focus rapidly from the steel ball’s trajectory to the surface of the transparent sphere. Composition places the curved shield surface in the foreground as a natural frame, mid-ground shows the impact point, and background features subdued audience area and gallery light strips. Under consistent neutral tones and soft lighting, sharper highlights appear at the moment of impact. The instant the steel ball strikes the sphere, the transition from intact to crack propagation to full explosion is fully recorded. Fragments of varying sizes eject outward along different arcs. Larger shards initially rush toward the shield before slowing and sliding down, while finer particles briefly shimmer with translucent quality under the lights. Background includes the base of the protective platform and blurred human silhouettes. Lighting remains soft and diffused, with only minimal cool glass reflections preserved on fragment edges, allowing lines and color blocks in the watercolor style to feel both controlled and dynamic. As the camera slowly pulls back, it re-incorporates the character, ground markings, fragment landing points, and protective platform into a single frame, ultimately freezing on a complete and readable ejection distribution map, concluding with the experiment result clearly observed and displayed.

prompts: Shot 1 begins with a fade-in, using a medium high-angle shot with slight zoom-in. Foreground shows the edge of a wooden workbench, midground focuses on an anthropomorphic lion entering the frame and placing a flowerpot, trowel, and seed packet onto the surface in sequence. Background is softly blurred, showing the museum atrium garden and tall columns. Moderate depth of field clearly highlights the instructional subject. Lighting is soft and even. A distinct table contact The shot ends with a stable view of neatly arranged tools, establishing a clear starting point for the next step.

Shot 2 follows the previous shot with a hard cut, using a close-up high-angle tight shot. The composition centers on the interior of an empty flowerpot. The foreground briefly captures the claw holding the trowel, while focus clearly tracks the falling stones and soil. First, small stones are laid at the bottom to form a distinct drainage layer, followed by loose nutrient soil being poured in, gradually raising the soil level. Despite the watercolor texture, the material contrast between rolling stones and pouring soil remains clearly distinguishable. The camera performs minimal downward tilt and fixed tracking to ensure viewers accurately observe the sequence.

Shot 3 transitions via action-matched editing from the prior shot, using a close-up eye-level slightly high-angle shot. The subject first gently levels the soil surface, then uses fingertips or a small tool to press several rows of evenly spaced shallow holes into the top layer. Soil transforms from loose and uneven to flat and orderly, with consistent spacing and depth of holes. Soft daylight maintains stable neutral brightness. Distant museum crowd murmurs persist but remain unobtrusive. The camera follows the hand horizontally, then slightly zooms in, allowing viewers to clearly understand the precision required in soil preparation before sowing.

Shot 4 cuts sharply from the previous shot, transitioning to a tight close-up high-angle shot. Composition is tighter, focusing on the seed packet opening, hand movements, and shallow hole positions. The anthropomorphic lion plants seeds one by one, each precisely landing in a hole, then gently covers with fine soil and lightly presses the surface with fingertip. The surface changes from visible holes to a softly filled, slightly raised state. Movements are smooth and rhythmically clear. The camera performs a very short zoom-in and pause, allowing “下种—覆土—轻压” three sub-steps to complete fully within a single shot.

Shot 5 continues into the next phase via a soft fade transition, using a medium-close eye-level shot. Foreground shows a label card and pen, background shows the flowerpot after sowing. The anthropomorphic lion first writes the sowing date on the label, then inserts it into the soil edge. Next, it picks up a narrow-spout watering can and slowly waters the soil thoroughly for the first time. After water falls, soil color gradually darkens, surface changes from loose dry to uniformly moist, with minor local sinking and absorption changes. Lighting remains soft and natural under the skylight. The camera first slightly shifts sideways to capture the date writing, then slowly tilts down to follow the water flow, ensuring both operational details and material changes are clearly visible.

Shot 6 connects to the previous shot via action-matched editing, cutting to a wide eye-level slightly low-angle shot. Foreground shows the flowerpot steadily held by both hands, midground shows the anthropomorphic lion walking toward a display rack on one side of the museum atrium, background reveals the glass skylight and open space of the public science garden. The subject places the pot under the skylight but not directly exposed to sunlight, and uses hand gestures to indicate maintaining diffused light and occasional watering—completing the final step from sowing to care instructions. Distant crowd murmurs become slightly clearer again. A soft placement The camera smoothly pans with the subject, then gently pulls back, ending the entire tutorial in a calm, tidy, and instructive-completion atmosphere.

The overall tone remains warm orange-red cyberpunk, with localized lighting from flame reflections and roadside screens. Soft daylight mixed with sugar surface reflections makes the entire forest translucent and radiant. A big-eyed fairy leaps from the foreground into the edge of the stream, running joyfully toward that glimmer. A warm golden side light sweeps across the end of the root, precisely revealing the metal outline of the band and several prong settings. The ring remains partially hidden. Composition places the fairy on the left moving right, positioning the band’s silhouette in the right highlight zone as the chase target. The camera first slightly pushes in, then subtly tilts up, amplifying the shock of the diamond’s expansion.

Shot 3 transitions naturally from the previous shot via a doorway framing cut, panning into the crystal hall, medium shot, eye-level perspective. Shot 4 cuts hard to the lava window, close-up low-angle composition. Shot 7 transitions via a pull-down page-style transition to the unboxing scene, medium-close shot, eye-level angle. Foreground shows a pair of hands placing the packaging box on a table, the box positioned centrally but slightly lower in the frame. prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in from black, using a wide-angle low-angle composition. In the foreground, the edge of a massive slowly rotating gear partially obscures the view. In the midground, a lion with metallic mane stands at the center of an elevated gear bridge. The background features layered steam-powered buildings, neon pipes, and steel skybridges extending into the distance. Leading lines formed by rivets and light strips on the bridge converge toward the subject. The depth of field is moderately deep to ensure clarity of the mechanical city environment. Warm orange-red neon reflections cast from the side of the buildings illuminate the scene, while high-contrast side lighting defines the metallic edges of the lion's mane. Occasional bursts of steam erupt from beneath the bridge, momentarily enveloping the lion in mist. The lion initially lowers its head, gathering momentum, then steps forward across the bridge. Its paws cause slight vibrations in the bridge surface, and the metallic plates of its mane and chain ornament at the tail sway rhythmically with each step. The gears beneath the bridge rotate in sync, demonstrating physical follow-through. Initially, the text extends along the bridge surface, then ascends staggered onto the facades of the surrounding buildings. The edges of the letters glow with orange electrical arcs and faint steam refractions, arranged in varying heights to create a sense of urban billboard pressure. When 'rust' is sung, a burst of steam shoots from a crack in the bridge.

The second shot cuts abruptly from the previous one and quickly pushes into a close-up, moving inside the Mechanical Core Plaza. The composition is a close-up at eye level with a slight upward angle: in the foreground, translucent steam drifts across the frame along with rotating copper pipes brushing the edges; the midground focuses on the lion's head, shoulders, neck, and front paws; the background reveals a radial mechanical space composed of multi-layered circular fans, pressure gauges, piston rods, and steam valves. Lighting continues the warm cyberpunk aesthetic from the prior shot, but high-contrast side lighting is more intensely focused on the lion's face and metallic mane. Copper reflections and backlighting along the steam edges amplify the explosive power of the roar. prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide-angle upward composition. The foreground features swirling golden clouds and translucent energy mist, the midground shows a suspended jade platform, and the background displays layered palace silhouettes and glowing runes. Warm orange neon glows from the platform edges and eaves, highlighting the lion's metallic mane with edge light, while its body reflects gently flowing rune-like highlights. It walks steadily to the platform edge, and its claws strike the surface with a clear, heavy metallic thud. The surrounding air trails concentric rings of orange-gold afterimages and fine particles. The camera slowly pushes in from the upward angle with slight tilt tracking, guiding the orb swiftly downward from the top of the frame.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut, transitioning to the floating track area below. The background remains the same warm orange cloud sea and suspended palace structure, ensuring spatial continuity. Lighting continues the previous neon volume and contour highlights, with stronger flickering reflections added only during impact to emphasize metallic texture and experimental key moments. The bright orb enters from the top of the frame and collides with the stationary metal ball, producing a brief, controlled orange-white impact flare. Before contact, the metal ball remains completely still; during contact, its surface exhibits high-frequency micro-vibrations and shimmering highlights; after contact, it clearly shows “一停一动”: the orb visibly decelerates and stops, while the cart is propelled forward along the track, its wheels scraping against the rails with a more intense metallic screech. At the same time, a holographic data interface beside the track flashes rapidly, displaying “动量守恒” in semi-transparent orange-gold text in the upper right corner, with numerical bars and vector arrows updating synchronously. The mecha-maned lion leans into the frame from the upper platform to observe the result, its mane tips vibrating slightly due to the downward airflow. The camera first slightly pulls back to stabilize in the eye-level close-up, then performs a short lateral pan along the track to follow the cart’s motion, finally stopping on the still-glowing holographic data and the moving apparatus, fully encapsulating the experimental outcome, object state changes, and mytho-cyber environment within a single frame.
