prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, long-distance overhead composition capturing both the celestial mountain range rising from swirling clouds and a crimson volcano. In the foreground, a smooth jade platform holds the focus—the teacup with limbs standing at its edge. Soft daylight outlines the paradise, while the volcano emits subtle warm pulses. The teacup stands still, gazing forward, arms slightly tensed, porcelain walls gently clinking in the wind. The camera slowly pushes in. A low alarm bell rings from afar, foreshadowing the coming upheaval.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning from full-frame eye-level to a medium-long tracking shot. In depth, the mountain’s belly deep within the clouds begins to glow. The teacup sprints along the path, limbs moving rapidly, body trembling slightly with each step. It suddenly turns back to look behind. The camera tracks laterally, matching its motion.

Shot 3 transitions via a quick whip cut into a close-up eye-level push-in. Composition focuses on the upper half of the teacup and its rim. Background blurs into soft teal-red streaks due to speed. Shallow depth of field draws attention to fine droplets forming on the rim and the rapid rise and fall of its body. the final consonant release aligns with a distinct exhale. The camera continues a gentle push closer.

Shot 4 follows with a hard cut, transitioning to an overhead mid-long shot. The camera hovers above a rift. Ancient rune-carved ground cracks from the center, golden-red lava violently pushing up through fissures. Cracks spread rapidly along the runes. Foreground rocks tumble down. Escape route remains visible at the end of the steps in the background. Diffused daylight is stained bright orange-red by the surging lava below. The camera performs a slight tilt-down.

Shot 5 follows with a motion-matched hard cut. A wide lateral tracking shot reveals a swaying rope bridge. Diagonal ropes in the foreground create pressure. Below, molten flow churns and heat waves rise. The teacup charges onto the bridge, leaning forward, arms swinging wider. Wooden planks bounce under weight and vibration, causing noticeable vertical oscillation of the cup. The camera moves rapidly along the bridge with slight shake, enhancing instability. Crisp porcelain clinks precisely sync with each footfall.

Shot 6 follows with a quick hard cut into a side close-up. Camera position slightly low, slight upward angle. Ruined eaves of an ancient temple and a violently ringing bronze bell dominate the background. At the moment the bell strikes, rocks cascade down from above. The teacup launches powerfully from the broken steps, limbs extended, tracing a brief arc in the air. Decorative fabric-like details and dust are lifted by airflow. Lava reflections flash rapidly across its smooth porcelain surface. The camera locks briefly, then slightly tilts up to follow the jump trajectory. The bell’s thunder and falling stones hitting the ground further amplify tension.

Shot 7 transitions via landing action match. Low-angle medium-close shot facing the volcanic vent. Composition shows black smoke and fire columns erupting from background to sky. The teacup is positioned slightly off-center in the lower frame. Heat waves in the foreground distort the air. Strong backlight from the volcano burns a bright outline around its silhouette. After landing, it immediately raises an arm to shield itself, pushed back half a step by the impact. Condensation on its surface evaporates instantly under high heat.

Shot 8 transitions via a brief fade-out and fade-in for emotional shift. Pulls back to long-distance eye-level. The entire paradise is bathed in fierce red light. Cloud edges are lit by fire. Mountains, temple, broken bridge, and rift form a complete disaster landscape. The teacup stands atop a cliff, silhouetted against the light. Limbs steady, facing the roaring inferno ahead. Foreground glows with hot light; background shows rising smoke columns and sparks. Unified crimson-gold backlight dominates, concluding the emotional arc. The camera slowly pulls back and slightly elevates, making the character appear small yet resilient against vast nature.

", perfectly synchronized with turning on the faucet and grabbing the wet towel.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in from black, using a wide aerial composition. Floating ash in the foreground and ground-hugging blue fog in the midground compress spatial depth. The scene is set in a forest devastated by wildfire, under cold blue ambient light covering the burnt earth surface, with faint orange glow from the distant fireline. No subject appears yet, allowing viewers to first sense the scale of the fire and wind direction. Wind pushes smoke layers low and sliding, while the fireline expands slowly in the distance. The camera slowly descends with a slight forward dolly, creating a sense of doom pressing down.

Shot 2 hard cuts from previous shot, using a near eye-level angle. A dog with a mechanical prosthetic eye stands beside a tilted abandoned road sign. The sign occupies the left foreground, the subject centered-right, focus on its head and the ash-covered ground near its front paws. Background includes smoldering logs and rolling smoke. Lighting remains cool blue, with faint red-orange firelight reflected at the edge of the mechanical eye. The dog lowers its body, ears alert, nose close to the ground sniffing ash, front paw lightly touching broken charcoal, stirring fine dust—indicating cautious path assessment. Mood stays tense and controlled. Camera performs a slight lateral pan and subtle push-in, emphasizing the subject’s alertness.

Shot 3 hard cuts from previous shot, using a medium side-follow tracking shot. The cracked highway extends from bottom-left to right-front, forming a strong vanishing point. The dog accelerates from the left toward a collapsed overpass ahead. Occasional burnt leaves blown by wind pass across the lens in the foreground. Midground shows the running subject; background features tilted bridge structure and broken railings. Cold blue smoke still covers low altitudes, with intermittent flames along the roadside. The dog’s run is clearly defined—shoulders rise and fall, limbs alternate powerfully, tail held low. The mechanical eye remains steadily illuminated during motion. Camera smoothly tracks sideways with slight shake, highlighting speed and spatial displacement during escape.

Shot 4 transitions from previous shot via rapid wipe, using a close-up eye-level shot. Focus tightly locked on the dog’s mechanical eye and half-face. Fine hairs and dust blur at the foreground edge; background compressed into blurred fiery spots. In the cool tone, the mechanical lens reflects flames climbing a dead tree. Gray particles and tiny scratches cling to the metal frame. The dog pauses briefly, pupils constrict, facial muscles tighten instantly—capturing the moment it detects sudden danger ahead. Camera slightly pushes in and locks focus, delivering a visual impact of perception and warning.

Shot 5 hard cuts from previous shot, using a close-up low-angle shot. The dog’s silhouette flashes sideways in the lower frame, while a massive burned branch crashes down from an upper diagonal. Composition uses the falling branch’s trajectory to split the frame. Background features broken bridge and burning dead trees forming intersecting lines. Flame flickers dimly in smoke. Cold blue smoke still envelops space but is torn open by orange-red fire. Subject action reaches explosive peak: back legs push off, body lunges forward. Falling branch kicks up sparks and ash, crushed charcoal scatters from impact. Mood shifts from oppression to sudden peril. Camera tilts up slightly then rapidly follows the fall path, intensifying the sense of imminent danger.

Shot 6 transitions from previous shot via smoke-filled matte wipe, using a medium-close eye-level push-in shot. Scene shifts to the entrance of a half-collapsed drainage tunnel. Foreground shows broken concrete and twisted rebar. Midground: dog lowers body and crawls into the tunnel. Background: firelight flickers outside the entrance. Tunnel interior is damp, cold, and blue-tinted; orange reflections from external flames dance at the entrance edge, forming unified yet subdued dual lighting. Dog’s movement shifts from high-speed escape to low-crawling advance. Shoulder brushes stones, fur on back ripples and blurs under incoming smoke. Smoke flows backward along the ceiling, gradually swallowing the entrance outline. Camera continuously pushes from outside the entrance into the tunnel, creating temporary refuge but greater suffocating pressure.

Shot 7 hard cuts from previous shot, using a medium-long low-eye-level pull-out shot. The dog bursts out from the other end of the drainage tunnel. Foreground: cracked slope and charred grass. Midground: subject sprints at high speed. Background: entire forest now connected into a web of fire, burning trunks lined up behind smoke layer. Cold blue smoke still covers the sky, but orange-red fire net brightness significantly increases, visually upgrading the disaster to full chaos. Dust on the dog’s body flings off, gravel kicks backward—indicating successful passage through narrow escape route and re-exposure to broader, more dangerous fire edge. Camera briefly follows then quickly pulls back, capturing both the subject’s smallness and the vast fire behind.

Shot 8 transitions from previous shot via slow fade-in, using a long slightly low-angle static hold. The dog’s silhouette stands on a ruin hill in the lower third of the frame. Foreground: broken metal and charred rocks. Midground: stationary subject. Background: entire sky swallowed by interwoven cold blue smoke and orange-red embers. Lighting continues consistent tone: cold color dominates overall temperature, edge firelight only outlines subject silhouette and faint reflection in mechanical eye. Action shifts from escape to brief pause: chest rises and falls, ear tips twitch, tail hangs low—showing high alertness but completion of this leg of journey. After slight pull-back, camera fully stops, freezing the relationship between apocalyptic ruins and lone survivor into the final image.

In the foreground, dark shadows of rocks are sliced by rain streaks; midground features walls and towers; distant sea occasionally outlined by lightning. Storm clouds press low on the horizon. Warm golden window lights stand out against the cold dark background, emphasizing the observation tower's seaside position, seemingly awaiting something. Wind drives flags and sea mist horizontally across the frame. The camera slowly pushes in from above, establishing environment and sense of danger.

Shot 2 cuts hard to an interior scene. A full shot at eye level captures a young woman holding a lantern as she walks through a stone corridor. Candles on both sides create repeating perspective lines leading toward a dark archway ahead. Foreground candles are slightly blurred; stained glass windows in the background tremble slightly under heavy rain. Warm candlelight outlines her figure. Brief flashes of cold blue lightning from outside briefly illuminate the stone walls. She moves cautiously, her cloak hem lifted gently by crosswind. Lantern light flickers on the wall, elongating her shadow. The camera follows her backward along the corridor with slight pan, creating a sense of forward pull toward the unknown.

The character is positioned slightly right and lower in frame, her lantern a warm light point in the rotating space. The observation tower’s inner walls are damp and weathered. Narrow arrow slits let in strong wind, which creates hollow echoing in the tower cavity. She descends steadily, one hand on the wall, one holding the lantern. Her pace shifts from cautious to increasingly drawn forward. The flame tilts sideways in the wind. Water puddles on the edge of the steps reflect faint glimmers. The camera follows from above along the spiral path, then slightly tilts to enhance the sensation of descent.

Shot 4 cuts hard with matching motion into the rune-filled water hall. It begins as a medium-wide eye-level push-in. Foreground shows a partially opened ancient stone door. prompts: Shot 1 opens directly with a wide eye-level shot. Chicken cubes, green onions, ginger, garlic, cucumber, peanuts, and seasoning bowls are neatly laid out. The background features a bright, clean kitchen cabinet and stove. Warm natural light evenly illuminates the surface.

Shot 2 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, switching to a medium close-up overhead view. The cutting board dominates the frame, with ingredients arranged in sequence across foreground and background. Focus remains locked on the intersection of hands and knife blade. The kitchen background is de-emphasized to maintain instructional clarity. Warm lighting remains consistent. The chicken is cleanly diced into uniform cubes, followed by separate cuts of green onions, ginger, garlic, and cucumber. She simultaneously explains “鸡肉切丁，葱姜蒜和黄瓜分别备好”. The camera remains mostly static, with only minimal follow pan to ensure full visibility of actions.

Shot 3 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, using a close-up overhead view. A glass bowl is centered in the frame, with spoons and seasonings in the foreground and a softly blurred background preserving countertop texture. Lighting remains warm and soft, creating clean reflections on the bowl’s surface. The young woman adds salt, cooking wine, and starch to the chicken, then rapidly mixes by hand. The chicken transitions from loose to moist and evenly coated. Precise interaction between fingers and ingredients is clearly visible. The camera performs a slight push-in to emphasize textural changes.

Shot 4 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, transitioning to a medium close-up overhead view. A small seasoning bowl is centered in composition. Sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, and a small amount of starch are added sequentially, forming clear procedural layers. Background remains the same countertop environment, with unchanged lighting. Liquids are stirred with chopsticks, quickly blending from layered to uniformly translucent. The camera performs a slight overhead circular movement to help viewers observe the mixture state.

Shot 5 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, shifting to a medium close-up slightly angled downward. The stove and pot opening occupy the right side of the frame, with a strainer and empty plate on the left for depth. Side lighting highlights the pot edge and peanut surface. The young woman pours peanuts into hot oil on low heat, gently frying them. Peanuts move slightly in oil, turning more golden. They are quickly scooped out with a strainer and removed. She explains “花生小火炸香，先盛出来保持脆感”. The camera performs a short lateral pan along the pot edge, then gently pushes in to emphasize heat control.

Shot 6 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, using a medium eye-level slightly side-angle view. The pot surface becomes the absolute focal point. The edge of the spatula appears in the foreground, while the background stove remains simple. Under warm light, the oil surface reflects soft, bright highlights. After heating the pan and adding oil, dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns are added. The spices jump rapidly in oil, releasing aroma and instantly activating their color. She clearly announces in Chinese “锅里留底油，下干辣椒和花椒，小火爆香”. The camera performs a slight tilt-follow from the pot edge, enhancing the layered impact of spices hitting the oil.

Shot 7 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, switching to a medium close-up slightly upward angle with a noticeable push-in. After chicken is added to the pot, it occupies the center of the frame. Steam and spatula form dynamic foreground obstructions. Background kitchen lights blur into soft warm spots. The chicken rapidly changes from translucent to opaque and shiny, edges slightly curling. Sleeve and steam follow movements realistically. The camera continuously pushes forward, reinforcing the sense of speed and transformation during stir-frying.

Shot 8 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, employing a composite motion from overhead to eye-level. Composition guides diced cucumber, peanuts, and sauce entering the pot from the top of the frame. Ingredients inside the pot form distinct color layers. Warm main lighting remains consistent, creating wet reflections on the sauce surface. The young woman quickly adds diced cucumber, returned peanuts, and prepared sauce. The spatula continuously flips ingredients, efficiently mixing them over high heat. Cucumber retains crispness, peanuts stay firm, and sauce begins to adhere. The camera first slightly lowers, then follows the stir-fry direction with a lateral pan, emphasizing critical heat control in the tutorial.

Shot 9 connects with the previous shot via match-cut editing, transitioning to a close-up eye-level view. A partial section of the pot fills the frame. Shallow depth of field keeps focus firmly on chicken and sauce surface. Background is fully blurred into warm color blocks. Sauce transitions from flowing to thickened, bubbles become finer, and glossy sheen evenly coats chicken, cucumber, and peanuts. Material changes are clearly discernible. She slows her pace, stating “看到汤汁收亮、均匀挂住食材就可以了”. The camera performs a macro-style slow push-in, clearly conveying the crucial pre-completion state.

Shot 10 gently dissolves from the previous shot, using a medium-long shot at eye level that slowly pulls back. The finished dish is transferred from the wok to a white plate on a wooden table. In the foreground, the freshly plated Kung Pao chicken is displayed, while the background reveals the still-bright and warm kitchen environment. Finely chopped green onions are evenly sprinkled over the top as the final touch. A young woman stands in front of the wooden table, looking directly at the camera, and concludes with a natural and friendly tone “这样做出来鸡丁嫩、花生脆、口感酸甜微辣，关键就是花生先盛出，最后大火快速收汁”. The soft The camera slowly pulls back, fully revealing the finished dish, the person, and the surrounding environment, bringing the tutorial to a clear and satisfying conclusion.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in into a wide eye-level composition. Foreground shows the laid-out yoga mat, mid-ground features a young woman standing at the center of the mat, background includes the window-side training area, dumbbell rack, and resistance bands. Window frame and floor lines form natural leading lines, focusing on the relationship between the subject and the training space. Cool morning light enters from the side-rear, outlining the subject’s silhouette and equipment edges.

Shot 2 hard cuts from previous shot to a close-up eye-level view, framing the upper body and abdominal region. Subject is positioned slightly off-center in a third-rule composition, background blurred but retaining window outline. Lighting remains cool natural light with soft fill. She demonstrates proper stance while clearly explaining “脚踩稳，收腹，肩膀放松，吸气准备”.

Shot 3 hard cuts to an extreme close-up eye-level shot, focusing on shoulder-neck and arm range of motion. Background depth of field is shallower, with cool window light creating thin contour lines on skin edges. She begins shoulder-neck circles and arm-opening warm-up, first slowly rotating shoulders, then opening arms outward. Movements are smooth and rhythmically steady. The camera makes small lateral follow movements to keep joint actions centered.

Shot 4 hard cuts to a medium eye-level shot, showing full-body in frame. Foreground retains minimal floor space for depth, background remains clean gym room with cool natural window light. Focus is on hip-knee-ankle coordination. She fully demonstrates squats: hinging hips back, lowering slowly, pausing, then rising upright. Knee trajectory is stable without inward collapse. She emphasizes “下蹲吸气，起身呼气，膝盖跟脚尖方向一致” in Camera slightly tilts down then up, following center-of-mass shift.

Shot 5 connects via smooth transition hard cut to a medium lateral pan shot. Subject moves to mirror area. Mirror in background reflects body side profile, creating dual foreground-background observation. Focus locks on front knee, toe direction, and trunk stability. Cool lighting remains consistent, with only soft reflection at mirror edge. She steps forward into lunge, bending front and back legs sequentially before returning to standing. Movement repeats once to reinforce learning. Camera laterally follows, showing both front and side posture.

Shot 6 transitions via quick downward cut to an overhead shot. Viewpoint directly above the mat. Mat edges and hand-elbow positions form clear geometric composition. Subject’s body occupies vertical axis. Focus precisely on elbow-shoulder-back alignment. Natural light from one side casts diagonal shadows on mat, revealing true texture. She lowers into plank position: elbows down, shoulders aligned, core engaged, body straight from head to heels. Camera maintains slight pitch adjustment to keep key support points visible.

Shot 7 hard cuts to a close-up low-angle shot from front-side. Shallow depth of field blurs background equipment. Focus follows knee advancement and flat back posture. Cool lighting unchanged, but ground reflects subtle bright strip. She begins slow mountain climbers, alternating legs forward, maintaining steady pace. Shoulders remain still, back does not sag. She reminds “慢一点也没关系，腰背不要塌”. Camera performs short push-pull movements to highlight core engagement and control.

Shot 8 connects via soft fade cut to a medium-wide eye-level shot. Frame pulls back, subject lying supine on mat. Foreground shows raised knees and pelvis, background still reveals window-side training area. Spatial continuity is clear. Focus shifts from glute bridge peak to posterior chain stretch. Cool natural light forms clean bright stripes on floor. She completes one standard glute bridge: lifts pelvis, tightens glutes, pauses, then lowers. Then smoothly transitions into leg hug and hamstring stretch. Movement flow is fluid. She gives brief cue “抬起时夹紧臀部，放下后接腿后侧拉伸”. Camera first slightly pulls back, then stabilizes, making full transition visible. Exhalation synchronizes strictly with lowering and stretching phases.

Shot 9 fades in to conclude with a close-up eye-level shot by the window. Composition focuses on face, neck, and subtly rising chest. Background is blurred window frame and soft cool daylight. Shallow depth of field makes facial expression the sole focus. Key light remains natural side light, with soft fill preserving skin texture realism. She returns to window, gently places hands, slowly inhales then exhales. Expression is focused and encouraging.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a medium close-up eye-level shot. The subject is seated in front of a vanity mirror, with slightly blurred makeup brushes and skincare bottles in the foreground. The focus is on her clear, bare face and its reflection in the mirror. The background features warm-toned home decor and desk organization, with soft lighting spreading from the side-front, revealing natural skin texture. She gently raises her hand to indicate her facial condition, then points to the products on the table, clearly mouthing “今天做一个清透通勤妆，保留自然感”. The camera slowly pushes in, establishing the tutorial's goal and initial state.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a close-up overhead view with a slight first-person perspective, creating a continuous composition from the tabletop to the face. Focus initially lands on her fingers unscrewing the cap of a moisturizer, then follows to her cheeks and forehead. Skincare products on the table form leading lines, with shallow depth of field emphasizing the texture of lotion and primer. She presses the moisturizer into her palm and gently spreads it across her face, then dots primer onto her cheeks, forehead, and chin, narrating in Chinese “先保湿，再薄上一层隔离让后续更服帖”. The The camera slightly tilts down and pans to follow her hand.

Shot 3 enters with a hard cut matching the action, shifting to a close-up facial detail, using a near-eye-level shot. A sponge is held in the foreground, while the mirror background is softly blurred. Focus tightly follows the foundation application from the bridge of the nose to the cheeks. Under consistent warm lighting, foundation is dotted onto the face and evenly patted out with the sponge in rhythmic motions. Localized skin tone gradually unifies, surface becomes smoother while retaining natural texture. The camera gently pushes in and slightly pans right to emphasize the transition from partial to full-face coverage.

Shot 4 cuts hard from the previous shot, transitioning to a tighter close-up of the under-eye and nostril area, framed in a slight high-angle close-up composition. The center of the frame focuses on the alternating motion between the concealer brush and fingertip, while the background softens into warm, blurred color blocks. She precisely dabs concealer onto the inner corners of the dark circles and both sides of the nostrils, then gently blends it using a small brush and fingertip. The dullness gradually brightens and the redness softens visibly. The camera remains nearly static, with only a minimal push-in to emphasize fine details.

Shot 5 transitions via a hard cut into eyebrow tutorial, using a medium close-up at a slightly angled eye-level view. The mirror image and real person form a dual-layer composition, focus locked on the eyebrow shape and the eyebrow pencil in hand.

It begins with a close-up overhead view capturing the eyeshadow palette and brush picking up pigment, then smoothly transitions to a frontal close-up of the eyes. She blends light brown shadow into the crease, applies a deeper shade at the outer corner, carefully lines along the base of the lashes, and finally curls her lashes. The eye's definition becomes progressively more vivid, with lashes lifting into a graceful curve. The camera initially moves forward slightly, pauses briefly, then subtly tilts upward following the curling motion, enhancing the sense of sequential progression.

Shot 7 transitions from the previous shot with a soft dissolve into cheek enhancement, using a medium close-up eye-level shot. Composition balances both cheeks symmetrically, with a highlighter palette below forming a secondary guide. In the same soft warm light, she lightly sweeps blush on the outer apples of the cheeks, then uses a small brush to add highlight to the bridge of the nose and cheekbones. Her complexion visibly becomes softer and more radiant, with controlled natural glow on the skin surface.

Shot 8 cuts sharply from the previous shot into a close-up of the lips, using an eye-level extreme close-up. Background maintains consistent warm tone and shallow depth of field. The camera slightly pushes in, then stabilizes gently, highlighting the final step before completion.

Shot 9 concludes with a soft dissolve from the previous shot, using a medium shot at eye-level with a slight mirror-facing composition. On the left, either a small inset of her original bare face or a head turn creates a before-and-after comparison; on the right, the completed makeup is shown directly. Focus is on the overall clear, unified finish and facial expression change. Background remains the same vanity area, warm lighting stable, avoiding stylistic jumps. The soft The camera first slightly pulls back to establish the full view, then gently pushes back to freeze-frame on the before-and-after contrast, forming a complete narrative loop.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide eye-level shot to present a clean woodworking workshop in full view. In the foreground, a workbench holds a tape measure, square, pencil, and clamps; the midground features wooden boards awaiting processing, while the background reveals a table saw and storage wall. Moderate depth of field clearly separates the layers of tools. Warm yellow lighting blends with natural light from the window, creating a stable, realistic wooden atmosphere. A middle-aged male carpenter stands beside the workbench, raising his hand to indicate today's project, while Chinese The camera slowly pushes in to establish a sense of being on-site for instruction.

The second shot is a hard cut from the previous one, using a close-up at eye level, with composition focused on several pine boards on the workbench. Blurred tools in the foreground form leading lines, while the midground clearly captures hands selecting wood based on grain and thickness. Warm lighting remains consistent as a middle-aged male carpenter picks up two pine boards to compare their edges and flatness, pointing at the board edges with his fingers and measuring length and width with a tape measure. The Chinese The camera performs a slight lateral follow, emphasizing the material selection logic.

Shot 3 cuts hard to a close-up overhead shot. The center of the frame is a flat wooden board, with ruler and pencil forming clear horizontal and vertical guides. Shallow depth of field sharpens scale markings and pencil tip. Under warm indoor lighting, wood grain details are visible. Chinese The scratch The camera maintains stable overhead framing with slight downward pressure to reinforce procedural rigor.

Shot 4 cuts hard to a close-up eye-level slightly low-angle shot, focusing on the clamp, board edge, and contact point with the workbench. Foreground shows the clamp knob, midground the board, background softly blurred. Warm lighting remains consistent. The carpenter tightens the clamp to secure the board firmly. The board slightly depresses under pressure before stabilizing. The camera performs a very short push-in to emphasize completion of the securing action.

Shot 5 cuts hard to a medium close-up eye-level shot. Foreground shows the edge of the safety guard, midground the hands feeding the board, background the wood shavings collection zone. Under warm lighting, metal and wood textures are distinct. Chinese The high-speed saw The camera smoothly tracks horizontally with the board’s motion, clearly showing the cutting path.

Shot 6 cuts hard to a close-up eye-level shot. The newly cut edge of the board dominates the frame. Foreground shows the plane blade edge, midground the hand’s pressure point, background softly blurred into warm workshop tones. Consistent side lighting casts soft highlights across the edge. The carpenter slowly pushes the plane to smooth the edge, thin shavings curling and falling onto the bench. The edge transitions from slightly rough to smooth. Chinese The planing The camera slightly follows the hand’s forward motion.

Shot 7 cuts hard to a close-up overhead slightly angled shot. Focus is locked on the drill bit and pre-marked hole. Foreground shows scattered wood shavings creating depth, midground the drill chuck and hands, background softly blurred. Warm lighting remains stable. The carpenter positions the drill bit vertically over the mark, lightly touching the wood before drilling in. Fine wood dust spreads in a ring. Chinese The brief startup The camera remains mostly static with minimal pitch correction.

Shot 8 cuts hard to a medium close-up overhead shot. The workbench serves as a flat background, with several cut boards forming the initial shape of a box. A square placed at one corner creates a clear visual focus. Moderate depth of field ensures each board’s edge is visible. Warm lighting remains consistent. The carpenter performs a dry fit without glue, placing side panels together one by one, then pressing the square against the inner corner to check for perpendicularity. The box transitions from scattered pieces to a stable upright structure. The camera slowly lowers slightly to make the right-angle check more visible.

Shot 9 enters the key step via a brief hard cut, using a medium close-up eye-level shot. Foreground shows the glue bottle opening, midground the joint, background unused clamps. Under warm lighting, the glue reflects finely. The carpenter evenly squeezes wood glue along the joint, then closes the boards and quickly applies clamps. Chinese The squeezing The camera first gently pushes toward the joint, then slightly pans to the clamps, fully showcasing the joining process.

Shot 10 cuts hard with a slight time jump, using a close-up eye-level shot. Focus is on the box’s corner and sandpaper contact surface after clamps are removed. Foreground shows fingers and folded sandpaper edge, midground the box edge, background softly blurred. Warm side lighting makes dust particles faintly visible. After removing clamps, the carpenter carefully sands along the edge. The surface transitions from slightly sticky with glue residue and splinters to uniformly smooth.

Shot 11 transitions softly with a fade-in/fade-out from the previous shot, using a medium close-up side angle shot. Composition aligns brush movement direction with the wood grain of the box. Foreground shows bristles, midground the side of the box, background a softly blurred warm workshop. Lighting remains primarily natural side light plus warm lamps. The carpenter dips a small amount of wood wax oil and applies it evenly along the grain. The surface gradually shifts from matte to warm and subtly glossy. Chinese The fine brushing The camera slowly pans to highlight the coating application process.

Shot 12 fades in from the previous shot, using a medium-long static wide-angle pull-back at eye level. The composition centers the completed minimalist wooden box on the workbench as the visual focal point, with a few neatly arranged tools in the foreground creating a sense of instructional closure. The midground features the finished product, while the background reveals a tidy workshop. Warm, soft lighting unifies the scene with gentle tones. The carpenter gently lifts the box with both hands and slowly turns it toward the camera to display its four sides and interior space. The surface is smooth, edges are crisp, and the wood has a warm, lustrous finish. A Chinese summary appears simultaneously “关键步骤就是量准、划准、切稳、先试拼再上胶，最后细磨和上油”.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a steady eye-level wide shot that slowly pushes in. A wooden table by the window is positioned slightly below center, creating a balanced composition. In the foreground, a neat tabletop holds several sheets of colored paper. The background features a window frame illuminated by warm sunlight and softly blurred indoor corners. The focus rests on the upper body of a young woman and the props on the table. She wears a natural smile, holding up a completed paper crane with her left hand and displaying a square sheet of colored paper with her right. The camera slowly moves forward, allowing viewers to clearly see the proportion between the material and the finished product. The paper gently trembles at her fingertips, and soft highlights form along the crease edges under the light.

The second shot cuts abruptly from the previous one, transitioning to an overhead close-up. The wooden grain of the tabletop spreads horizontally as a clear background, with a tight composition where the colored paper dominates the frame. In shallow depth of field, the hands and edges of the paper are most sharply defined. She carefully folds the square sheet of colored paper along its diagonal, slowly aligning the two corners and then pressing down from the center toward both ends with her fingertips to create a crisp crease, while softly explaining “先沿对角线对折，对齐四角，再把中间的折痕压实”. Warm natural light slants in from the upper left of the frame, casting shadows along the fold that help viewers perceive the structural change.

The third shot enters with a sharp cut from the previous one, using an overhead close-up with a slightly wider framing to fully capture the unfolding motion of both hands. The composition uses the central axis of the paper as a visual guide. The paper transitions from a triangular shape into a more three-dimensional diamond structure, while the Chinese The camera follows her hand movements with a subtle downward tracking motion, ensuring that each alignment, pinch, and smoothing action remains in focus.

Shot 4 connects to the previous shot with a soft, continuous motion cut, transitioning to a level close-up from a front-side angle that captures the crucial steps in forming the paper crane into a three-dimensional shape. In the foreground, her fingers steadily support the body of the paper crane, with focus placed on the tip and the crease junctions. The background window light is softly blurred into warm highlights. As she folds, she quietly explains in Chinese “现在把一端翻出颈部，另一端翻出尾部，折的时候慢一点，角度尽量对称”, gently pinching the lower part of the paper and pulling apart while flipping both ends in opposite directions, gradually creating a difference in length between the neck and tail sections. The camera performs a slight lateral pan and a subtle push-in, emphasizing the opening, folding, and shaping of the paper layers. Sharp creases become more pronounced under pressure, with clear and detailed movements shown without any skipped steps.

Shot 5 concludes with a soft fade-in/fade-out transition from the previous shot, using a close-up pull-back to capture the young woman returning naturally to her wooden desk by the window. The composition begins with her finished paper crane in hand, initially focusing on the crane's head and wings, then gradually pulling back to include her posture as she holds it up along with the tabletop. She gently spreads the wings fully, allowing the silhouette of the paper crane to unfold completely, then lifts it to chest height with both hands, smiling as she summarizes in Chinese “最后把翅膀轻轻展开，一只纸鹤就完成了，跟着步骤慢慢做就可以”. As the camera pulls back, viewers get a full view of the final result and the working environment.
